goal: `mc run --update` is something a person can trust: it says at once whether there is anything to update, what the runner is waiting on and for how long while it drains, and the same on the page and in the refusal `mc run start` gives; a drain is never silent for an hour; and a handover that fails leaves a runner running, never a dead process behind a live `runner.json`.
contract: Martin, 2026-10-07 (ruling 27): `--update` has to be robust enough that he stops force-stopping and restarting the runner by hand.

The drain stays as Martin chose it on 2026-09-04 (run.js `UPDATE drains the runner`, the comment at :2313): from the moment UPDATE is read no lane starts a step, the steps in flight finish and land, and the handover comes when nothing is in flight. Step 3 is the one that may change that, and it waits on his decision.
A step in flight is never killed by an update. Work the runner started lands or fails on its own terms.
out_of_scope: `mc run stop` and `stop --force` (run-control.js:194–231): they do what they say.
The lane counts and `mc run lanes` (lane-count.js).
What a step session does with a STOP that arrives during its wait (run.js:1807).

success_criteria.criterion: `mc run --update` on a runner already running origin/main's commit writes nothing and says so; on a draining runner it prints the drain — since when, which lanes are done and which are in a step with the project, step and elapsed time — instead of rewriting UPDATE; the page's MC line and `mc run start`'s refusal carry the same drain line.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/run-control.test.js`: the three answers of `requestUpdate` (nothing to update; UPDATE written; already draining, with the lanes listed from `current-*.json` fixtures); `tests/mc/page.test.js`: the MC line with a drain in progress names the lane it waits on and its elapsed time.

success_criteria.criterion: A draining runner writes a line to runner.log every ten minutes naming what it still waits on, a handover that cannot respawn keeps the runner running, and the quota pause ends the moment the runner is quiet under an UPDATE.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/run.test.js`: a drain across a step longer than ten minutes (fake clock) logs the waiting line with the step's name; a `handOver` that returns `{ ok: false }` leaves the loop running and the next pick happens; `quotaPause` with UPDATE and no current files returns before its sleep is over.

steps.title: `mc run --update` answers with the state, and writes nothing twice
steps.done_when: `requestUpdate` in `src/mc/run-control.js` has three answers — nothing to update (the runner's `commit` equals `origin/main` after a fetch), UPDATE written, already draining with the lanes listed — the drain line is one function shared by `requestUpdate`, `startRunner`'s refusal and the page's MC line, and `tests/mc/run-control.test.js` and `tests/mc/page.test.js` pin all of it.
instruction: What happened on 2026-10-07 evening (runner.log 72140–72200): UPDATE written 18:41 with six lanes busy; four lanes announced the drain as their steps landed (18:41, 18:42, 18:46, 18:48); nothing said what the other lanes were doing; at 18:56:24 Martin force-stopped and started a new runner (it started on `ad056b39`, which was origin/main), and at 18:56:41 wrote `--update` again — on a runner already current — which drained all six lanes once more. The two earlier drains took 29 min (2026-10-03 21:02→21:31) and 42 min (2026-10-05 20:06→20:48). `requestUpdate` (run-control.js:291–328) writes the file and prints two lines; it does not read `runner.json`'s `commit` (written by `markRunner`, run.js:2189–2192) and does not look at `current-*.json`; `startRunner` (:141–153) refuses a live runner with two lines; the page says `update requested N ago — the runner hands over after this round` (page-render.js:1013–1040).

Add to `run-control.js` a `drainState({ paths, read, list, now })` that returns: `requested` (the UPDATE file's timestamp, or null), `commit` (runner.json's), `inFlight` (one entry per `current-*.json`: `name`, the step number if the file carries it — read what `runStep` writes there, run.js:489 and the writer — `lane` from the file name, `started`, elapsed seconds) and `lanes` (the count from `lanes.json`, so done = lanes − inFlight). Add `drainLine(state)`: `draining since 18:56 (14 min) — waiting on gmail-ready step 1 (memoro#5, 14 min), claims-entity step 1 (memoro#2, 14 min); 6 lanes done`. `requestUpdate`: fetch origin in the mc checkout (`mcCheckout()`, :335; `deps.git` as `handOver` uses it) and compare `origin/main`'s short sha with `runner.json`'s `commit` — equal: print `runner pid N is already on <sha> — nothing to update` and write nothing (a `--force` flag writes anyway, for a restart that is wanted for another reason); UPDATE already present: print the drain line and write nothing; otherwise write and print as today plus the drain line. `startRunner`'s refusal and the page's MC line (page-render.js:1025–1040; the collector that feeds `info.update_requested` — find it by that name under `src/mc/`) use the same `drainLine`. `mc run --update` is parsed in `src/mc/commands/run.js:218–222`; add `--force` there.

Tests: `tests/mc/run-control.test.js` § 'mc run --update' (:226) gains the three answers with fixture files for runner.json (with `commit`), UPDATE and two `current-*.json`; `tests/mc/page.test.js` the MC line with a drain. `help-text.js` (the `mc run --update` lines, :14–21 of commands/run.js and the help block) say the three answers in one sentence each.

steps.title: The drain is never silent, a failed handover never exits, and the quota pause ends when quiet
steps.done_when: A draining lane loop writes `update: still waiting on …` every ten minutes with the in-flight steps (one line for the runner, not one per lane); `runLoop` keeps running when `update()` returns false and says why; `quotaPause` returns as soon as UPDATE is present and no `current-*.json` exists; `tests/mc/run.test.js` pins the three.
instruction: `run.js:2337–2344`: a draining lane polls `quiet()` every `UPDATE_POLL_MS` and says one line when it starts draining; nothing is said again until the handover, which on 2026-10-05 was 42 minutes later. Add a runner-level ticker (not per lane: six lanes would write six lines) that, while `updateRequested()` and not quiet, writes `update: still waiting on <drainLine's in-flight part>` every ten minutes, using `drainState` from step 1 so the words are the same ones `mc run --update` prints.

`run.js:2373–2375`: when `update()` returns false (`handOver` could not respawn, run-control.js:365–369), the loop falls through to `runner.say('runner exit — the update did not hand over'); return 0;` — the process ends with `runner.json` re-marked by `update()`'s `markRunner()`, so the page says a runner is running while none is, and the next `mc run --update` answers 'runner.json names pid N, which is gone'. Instead: remove the UPDATE file, say `update: could not hand over — this runner keeps going on <commit>; mc run --update to try again`, and re-enter the lane loops (restructure so the lanes are started by a function the loop can call again, or wrap the `Promise.all` in a `for (;;)` that breaks only on stop or a successful handover).

`quotaPause` (run.js:590–610) sleeps in `QUOTA_SLEEP_MS` slices and returns on STOP or UPDATE only at a slice boundary — 30 minutes. On 2026-10-07 18:30:58 'every lane sleeping 30m' and the UPDATE of 18:41 waited for the slice. Make the slice shorter under an update (poll `UPDATE_POLL_MS` while `updateRequested()`), and return at once when `updateRequested()` and the runner is quiet (`paths.currents().length === 0`): a quiet runner under an UPDATE has nothing to wait for. Tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js` next to 'UPDATE file: the loop finishes the step it is in' (:1554): the ticker line after ten fake minutes, the failed handover keeping the loop, the quota pause returning early.

steps.title: The successor starts at once and the old runner only finishes what it holds
steps.done_when: On UPDATE the runner respawns its successor at once (after the fast-forward); the successor starts every lane whose `current-<repo>-<lane>.json` is not held by a live predecessor and treats the predecessor's in-flight projects as claimed; the old runner takes no new step, finishes the passes it is in and exits without clearing the successor's files; `runner.json` names the successor with the predecessor's pid while they overlap and the page shows both; `tests/mc/run.test.js` and `tests/mc/run-control.test.js` pin the overlap, the lane wait, the claim and the exit.
instruction: Martin, 2026-10-07 (ruling 28): the successor starts at once on the lanes the old runner does not hold; the old runner only finishes what it holds. Today (run.js:2337–2344, 2280–2286, 2373) the drain waits for `quiet()` before `update()` clears `runner.json` and respawns. Change the order: when a lane first reads UPDATE, the runner (once, not per lane — guard with a flag beside `handedOver`) runs `handOver` immediately: the fast-forward as today (run-control.js:351–372), then `respawn`; the old runner keeps `runner.json` as is until the successor has written its own (see below), says `update: handed over to pid N — finishing <k> step(s) in flight, taking nothing new`, and its lanes go on exactly as the drain does now — a lane in a pass returns when the pass ends, an idle lane returns at once; when every lane has returned the process exits with `handedOver = true` (:2272–2275), which already skips `clearRunner()`, so the successor's `runner.json` and `current-*.json` are not removed by the old runner's exit. The ten-minute waiting line of step 2 now says what the *old* runner still holds.

The successor's start (run.js:2234–2241): `readRunner` names the old pid, alive, and the start refuses — add the one case it must accept: UPDATE was written by this handover (the respawn passes `MC_RUN_SUCCESSOR_OF=<old pid>` in the environment, read with `deps.env`) and the pid it names is that predecessor; then `markRunner` writes `{ pid, started, commit, predecessor: { pid, started } }` and the old runner is from then on only the parent of its sessions. `readRunner` (run-control.js:115–121) returns `predecessor` too; `mc run stop` ends both (the predecessor's group as well, `endNow`), `mc run start` refuses while either is alive, and the page's runner line (page-render.js, the MC line and the running section; `drainLine` from step 1) says `pid N on <commit> · pid M finishing 2 steps (gmail-ready, claims-entity)`. When the predecessor's pid is gone, the next `markRunner`-reader drops `predecessor` (the successor rewrites `runner.json` without it on its next chores pass).

Lanes and claims: the successor's lane `(repo, index)` must not start while `current-<repo>-<index>.json` exists with a live `pid` other than its own — `currentFor` (run.js:489) names the files; the file carries `pid` (the runner's, written by `runStep`) — so a successor lane polls `UPDATE_POLL_MS` until the file is gone, saying once `memoro#5: waiting for pid M to finish gmail-ready`. The predecessor's in-flight projects are claimed: `nextFor(... claimed: claims ...)` (run.js:2046) gets `claims` unioned with the `name`s read from every `current-*.json` whose `pid` is alive and not this process, so the successor never picks a project the old runner is landing (its step would otherwise be started twice: once by the old runner's merge, once by a fresh pick). The merge side needs nothing: the old runner's `landPr` claims the repository lease as any round does (ruling 26 and `deploy-beside-merges` cover the lease).

Tests: `tests/mc/run.test.js` next to 'UPDATE file: the loop finishes the step it is in' (:1554) — the handover happens before the in-flight step ends (the fake session is still running when `respawn` is called), the old runner exits only when the step's pass has ended and does not remove the successor's files; a successor fixture with a predecessor's `current-memoro-1.json` (live pid) waits for lane 1 and skips the named project in `nextFor`, then starts lane 1 when the file goes; `tests/mc/run-control.test.js`: `readRunner` with `predecessor`, `startRunner` refusing while either pid is alive, `stopRunner --force` ending both. `help-text.js` § `mc run --update` says the successor starts at once and the old runner finishes what it holds. Update the comment block at run.js:2313–2323 to state the new rule and cite ruling 28; the 2026-09-04 history stays in it.
